chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever you narrate a hadith, attribute it to the one who narrated it to you. For if it was true, it is to your credit; and if it was a lie, it is upon him.'

key_terms.أَسْنِدُوهُ: attribute/chain it — to trace a report back to its source through a chain of narrators (isnad)
key_terms.حَدِيث: hadith — a narration or report, specifically a saying or action attributed to a Prophet or Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about citing the source when narrating a hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) instructs that one must always cite the source of any hadith they transmit, attributing it to the narrator from whom they received it. This teaching establishes the foundational principle of isnad (chain of transmission) in Islamic hadith methodology, ensuring accountability: the transmitter gains merit for accurate narration and is absolved of responsibility for falsehood, which falls upon the originating fabricator. In early Islamic scholarship, as fabricated hadiths began to proliferate, this principle was essential for distinguishing authentic traditions from invented ones.
